Where it began

Darren Gough was born in Barnsley on 18 September 1970 and went to the Priory School there. Football nearly had him first: Rotherham United offered him a contract, but he picked cricket instead.

He made his first-class debut for Yorkshire in 1989, against Middlesex at Lord's, and took five wickets. Figures of 7 for 42 against Somerset earned him his county cap in 1993, and in 2001 he was part of the Yorkshire side that won the County Championship for the first time in 33 years.

The player

England picked him against New Zealand at Old Trafford in 1994. He took a wicket in his first over and made 65 with the bat. That winter in Australia he took 20 wickets at 21.25 and became the face of a hard tour.

He had many great days. At Headingley in 1998 he took 6 for 42 to seal England's first five-Test home series win since 1985. In Melbourne that winter he bowled MacGill and trapped McGrath to win the Test by 12 runs, then in Sydney he dismissed Healy, MacGill and Miller with consecutive balls for the first Ashes hat-trick by an England bowler in almost 100 years. In 2000 he took 25 wickets against the West Indies and shared the player of the series award with Courtney Walsh. In 58 Tests from 1994 to 2003 he took 229 wickets at 28.40, with nine five-wicket innings.

What made him special

He was not especially tall, but he ran in hard and leapt into a sideways-on action that made the ball skid on at the batsman. He swung it late, and his best ball was the inswinging yorker, which is why so many of his wickets were bowled or leg before. Everything he did came with energy and a grin, and in one-day cricket he became the first England bowler to reach 200 wickets.

The bat was more of a bonus. That 65 on debut was the highest score of his Test career, so he spent the next nine years trying to beat his own first day.

Away from the middle

He was a Wisden Cricketer of the Year in 1999, captained Yorkshire on his return to the county in 2007 and retired after the 2008 season, with Justin Langer his last first-class wicket. In 2005 he won Strictly Come Dancing with Lilia Kopylova, the first cricketer to do so, and he won two Christmas specials as well. He presented on talkSPORT from 2009, was Yorkshire's director of cricket from 2021 to 2024, and was made an MBE in 2020. He was best man at Kevin Pietersen's wedding and follows Barnsley football club.

And finally

In 2010 he became an ambassador for a strong Welsh cheddar, and duly turned up at the International Cheese Awards in Nantwich. Few fast bowlers have collected an Ashes hat-trick, a dancing title and a place among the cheeses.
